item.title: New Irish language community group launched in Cavan
item.description: Seachtain na Gaeilge got off to a lively start in Cavan yesterday evening with the official launch of ‘Gaelphobal an Chabháin’. The new community group a local branch of national Irish language advocacy organisation, Conradh na Gaeilge. says that this is a milestone for the language in Cavan. This year, Gaelphobal An Chabháin coordinated with local groups and organisations to put together a joint programme of up to 50 events for the annual festival, due to be published over the weekend. item.title: Man appears in court over thefts from Monaghan department store
item.description: A man appeared in court this week over stealing three coffee makers on three different dates from the same department store in Monaghan Town. Raivis Rozentals (24) carried out the thefts at Fleming's Department Store in Monaghan between January 12th and 17th, 2022. The three DeLonghi manufactured appliances were valued at €399 each. item.title: Local Enterprise Week set to begin across Cavan from Monday
item.description: Local Enterprise Office Cavan is set to launch its schedule of events to celebrate Local Enterprise Week 2026 which kicks off on Monday. The launch event for Local Enterprise Week will be held at the new IDA Building, Killygarry Business Park, Cavan. This event will focus on innovation in construction, engineering, advanced manufacturing, and sustainable construction in County Cavan. item.title: Drogheda United to pay Dundalk pitch repairs
item.description: Drogheda United have confirmed they will pay the full cost of repairing Dundalk’s pitch after last week’s Louth derby. The League of Ireland had imposed a €15,000 fine on the club after last Friday’s game; where Drogheda fans threw flares onto the Oriel Park pitch. The incident was heavily condemned by minister for sport Patrick O’Donovan who was in attendance.
